root_causes.root_cause: Arabic heading-marker regexes (_AR_PART_RE, _AR_ARTICLE_RE) in _inject_arabic_structural_headings() and numbering_depth() are insufficient for the specific heading formats used in UAE legal documents. They require the structural word (مادة/باب/فصل/قسم/جزء) at line START, but the Docling/remote OCR output for these documents formats headings differently (numbered prefixes, inline citations, or OCR formatting that prevents line-start matching). This leaves the tree flat (depth 0-1) because md_to_tree only nests based on markdown heading levels.
root_causes.suggested_fix: Extend _inject_arabic_structural_headings to handle additional UAE-legal heading formats: (1) numbered-prefix articles like '1. المادة' or Arabic-Indic '١. المادة', (2) parenthesized articles without the structural word at line start, (3) chapter/section words preceded by numbers/ordinals. Also expand _AR_ARTICLE_RE to match المادة in additional contexts (e.g., after bullet numbers). This needs to run both on the remote Docling service AND in client.py for remote-markdown post-processing.

root_causes.root_cause: No heading injection or numbering-depth recognition exists for English Book/Part/Chapter structural words, and _inject_english_article_headings only matches 'Article (N)' with parentheses, not 'Article N' without parentheses. The _NUM_PART_RE regex recognizes only German structural words (Teil/Anhang/Kapitel/Abschnitt), not their English equivalents. English legal documents using Book/Part/Chapter/Article hierarchy produce flat trees because these structural headings are never promoted from prose to markdown headings, and numbering_depth returns None for them.
root_causes.suggested_fix: (1) Add _inject_english_hierarchy_headings() that promotes 'Book N'/'Part N'/'Chapter N'/'Section N' lines to '#' headings (depth 1) and 'Article N' (without parens) to '##' headings (depth 2), with the same line-start anchor and char-limit guards as the Arabic and German injectors. (2) Expand _NUM_PART_RE to include English structural words: '^(?:Teil|Anhang|Kapitel|Abschnitt|Book|Part|Chapter|Section)\b'. (3) Expand _EN_ARTICLE_PROSE_RE to also match 'Article N' without parentheses (currently only matches 'Article (N)'). (4) Add corresponding calls in pdf_to_markdown_docling() alongside existing injectors.

root_causes.root_cause: When the remote Docling service path is used, client.py receives raw markdown and passes it to md_to_tree WITHOUT running the heading injection chain (_inject_arabic_structural_headings, _inject_english_article_headings, _inject_german_clause_headings) or heading-depth recovery (_recover_heading_depth, _relevel_by_containment, _relevel_by_numbering). These run ONLY inside pdf_to_markdown_docling() in converters.py. The remote Docling service should run its own copy of this chain, but if the remote service has a stale build (the B1-C1 issue from RFC-034 identified stale builds until 2026-08-07), or if the remote service does not include the latest heading injection improvements, the returned markdown will lack promoted headings and depth recovery, producing flat trees.
root_causes.suggested_fix: Add a post-processing step in client.py's remote path (after receiving markdown from the remote service, before feeding to md_to_tree) that runs _inject_arabic_structural_headings + _inject_english_article_headings + _inject_german_clause_headings + _pre_inference_normalize + _recover_heading_depth on the received markdown. This ensures heading injection runs regardless of the remote service's build version. Alternatively, confirm the remote service has the latest code and add version-gated fallback.
